source.name: National Conference of State Legislatures: Voter ID Laws

caveats: NCSL doesn't name states with no ID requirement; those are inferred from its tables, and Vermont's entry is unclear on the page. Rules change often.

states.name: Alabama
states.note: Provisional ballot; ID due by 5 p.m. Friday after the election, or two election officials' sworn affidavits. Digital IDs are barred from Oct. 1, 2026.

states.name: Alaska
states.note: Questioned ballot if no ID; an official may waive the requirement if they know the voter.

states.name: Arizona
states.note: Photo ID, or two non-photo documents; a provisional ballot needs ID by the deadline.

states.name: Arkansas
states.note: Provisional ballot; ID due by noon Monday after the election. Digital IDs allowed.

states.name: Colorado
states.note: Provisional ballot; applies to the few in-person voters, since most vote by mail. Digital IDs allowed.

states.name: Connecticut
states.note: Social Security card or preprinted ID; or a signed statement under penalty of false statement.

states.name: Delaware
states.note: "Proof of identity" with no defined list; signed affidavit if none.

states.name: District of Columbia
states.note: DC uses other verification methods.

states.name: Florida
states.note: Provisional ballot with signature matching. The accepted ID list narrows on Jan. 1, 2027.

states.name: Georgia
states.note: Provisional ballot; photo ID due within three days. Digital IDs barred.

states.name: Idaho
states.note: An affidavit is allowed; it must include date of birth or an ID number (2026 change).

states.name: Indiana
states.note: Provisional ballot; affidavit exception for indigent or religious objection. School IDs barred.

states.name: Iowa
states.note: Provisional ballot; ID due by noon Monday after the election. The affidavit-by-another-voter option was removed in 2026.

states.name: Kansas
states.note: Provisional ballot; ID to the county officer before canvass. Limited exemptions.

states.name: Kentucky
states.note: Affirmation form plus a reason and an acceptable ID document; care-facility residents exempt.

states.name: Louisiana
states.note: Affidavit allowed until July 1, 2027, then removed; more ID types added.

states.name: Michigan
states.note: Voters without photo ID can sign an affidavit and vote a regular ballot.

states.name: Mississippi
states.note: Affidavit ballot; photo ID due within five days. Religious-objection exemption.

states.name: Missouri
states.note: Provisional ballot; ID by 7 p.m. same day, or signature match.

states.name: Montana
states.note: Provisional ballot; signature verification. Some student IDs accepted.

states.name: Nebraska
states.note: Provisional ballot; reasonable-impediment certification; ID due by Friday after the election.

states.name: New Hampshire
states.note: Poll-worker verification; a denial can be appealed to superior court. Student IDs dropped after June 2, 2026.

states.name: North Carolina
states.note: Provisional ballot; ID due by the business day before canvass. Several exceptions.

states.name: North Dakota
states.note: Ballot set aside; ID due by the sixth day after the election. Special rules for long-term care and military.

states.name: Ohio
states.note: Provisional ballot; ID due within four days. Religious-objection affidavit available.

states.name: Oklahoma
states.note: The county voter registration card can serve as ID; provisional ballot checked against registration data.

states.name: Oregon
states.note: Oregon votes by mail.

states.name: Rhode Island
states.note: Provisional ballot; signature must match registration.

states.name: South Carolina
states.note: Reasonable-impediment option; otherwise a provisional ballot with ID due before certification.

states.name: South Dakota
states.note: An affidavit under penalty of perjury is accepted in lieu of ID.

states.name: Tennessee
states.note: Provisional ballot; ID due by the second business day. Indigent or religious affidavit option. Digital IDs barred.

states.name: Texas
states.note: Reasonable-impediment declaration; photo ID due within six days.

states.name: Utah
states.note: Provisional ballot; the clerk may verify identity by other means; some ID due by Monday after the election.

states.name: Virginia
states.note: Regular ballot after a signed perjury statement; provisional ballot if neither ID nor statement.

states.name: Washington
states.note: Signed declaration or ID; applies to in-person vote centers, since most vote by mail.

states.name: West Virginia
states.note: Changed from non-photo to photo ID in 2025; provisional ballot with affidavit and signature check. Known-voter vouching option.

states.name: Wisconsin
states.note: Provisional ballot; ID due by 4 p.m. Friday after the election.

states.name: Wyoming
states.note: Medicare/Medicaid cards accepted until Dec. 31, 2029. Provisional ballot; ID due next business day. NCSL's own sources conflict on whether this counts as photo ID.
